title: VendPoint Field Service Standard — Restocking, Consigned Stock and Cycle Counts
content:
Field service standard for stock in machines of the VendPoint Industrial Vending Program.

**S1 Restocking.** Corbett restocks each machine the model's scheduled number of restock visits a week, filling every selection at or below the model's low-stock trigger percent of par back to par, without letting the machine stock value exceed the model's machine stock cap; an emergency restock on request is made within the model's emergency response hours.

**S2 Ownership.** Machine stock stays Corbett-owned under the model's consigned inventory setting until vended.

**S3 Cycle counts and shrink.** Every cycle count interval, in months, the stock is counted; where the model bills shrink to the customer the shortage value above the shrink tolerance percent of the stock value counted is billed at the shrink billing basis in that month's usage bill, and where it does not Corbett absorbs all shrink.

**S4 Withdrawals.** Stock is withdrawn at no charge when a selection is removed, when overstock exceeds the cap, and when the machine is removed.

### Machine stock value

The machine stock value is the value, at contract unit price, of Corbett-owned consigned stock loaded in the machine: restocks and returns to the machine increase it; vends, shrink billed and withdrawals decrease it.

### S1 and S3 as judgements

| Fact | Result |
|---|---|
| Selection fill level at or below the low-stock trigger percent of par | Filled back to par at the visit, within the machine stock cap |
| Selection fill level above the trigger | Not filled under S1 |
| Model bills shrink, shortage above tolerance | The part above tolerance is billed in that month's usage bill |
| Model does not bill shrink | Corbett absorbs all shrink |

### Hypothetical figures

On a model with a 25% trigger, a selection with a par of 20 units is filled at a visit when it stands at 5 units (25% of par) or fewer, and is not filled at 6 units. On a model with a 1.5% tolerance, a count of 10000.00 USD of stock absorbs 150.00 USD of shortage; a shortage of 200.00 USD bills 50.00 USD at the shrink billing basis. The figures are invented.
